resale_co.name: Occupancy Certificate (Continued Occupancy Certificate)
resale_co.issued_by: City of Passaic Inspections & Code, Division of Housing
resale_co.lead_time: Apply at least 2 weeks before closing. If the inspection passes and all final approvals are in, the Continued Occupancy Certificate is issued in 5 to 7 business days; expedited service (5 days or less) costs $300.00 extra.
requirements: Inspection for compliance with Passaic's property maintenance and zoning laws
Buyer's full contact information on the application (otherwise it is put on hold); the certificate is issued in the buyer's name
Companies buying must give the registered agent's name and a copy of the certificate of formation
Buyer signs a notarized Purchaser's Form agreeing that the cellar is used only for storage (no sleeping, dwelling or rooming use, no partition walls)
Fire Prevention smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm certification is part of the occupancy certificate requirements
Vacant properties are inspected even without utilities and must stay vacant until violations are fixed and permits are finalized with the Building Department
Cancel inspections at least 24 hours ahead; open applications are voided 60 days after the compliance date

fees.label: Expedited certificate (5 days or less), in addition to the certificate fee
fees.quote: Expedited Certificates ( for Continued OC or TCO): o This service fee is $300.00 and completed within five (5) days or less.

fees.label: Re-inspection after a missed appointment or when fewer than 60% of units can be inspected ($50 or $20 per unit, whichever is less)
fees.amount: $50 or $20 per unit, whichever is less
fees.quote: the applicant will be required to pay a re-inspection fee of $50 or $20 per unit, whichever is less.

fees.label: Smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm certification, initial inspection

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Division of Housing Occupancy Certificate Application for a one family or two family home (seller, buyer and room details, signed affidavit), plus the notarized Purchaser's Form and the Fire Prevention Application for Fire Certification. Submit to the Division of Housing, City Hall, 330 Passaic Street, with the fee by money order, check or cash. Inspection and violation reports are emailed to the seller and buyer.

resale_co.notes: Passaic's Division of Housing issues an Occupancy Certificate (Continued Occupancy Certificate) on sale, checking property maintenance and zoning; it does not replace construction permits. Fees are from the City's current application forms (one family $65.00, two family $100.00; forms modified March 2026); the condo application is separate. A search result described Ordinance No. 2515-26 (final adoption February 17, 2026) as setting $65 for the first unit and $35 for each unit 2 through 20, which matches the forms, but the ordinance PDF links on the City site now return 'not found', so the ordinance text itself was not read. A Temporary Occupancy Certificate (escrow based on violations, issued in 2 to 3 business days, valid 30 days) is available. Changing the buyer's name after 30 days needs a new application and fees. Rentals are separate: tenant registrations with the Division of Housing (fee waived within 30 days of the certificate, otherwise $25.00 per unit), and a yearly heating system inspection certification (Ordinance 2339-22). Emails are taken from the mailto links on the Housing page.

requirements: Smoke detectors and CO detectors on each level (basement, first and second floors; not crawl spaces or unfinished attics), battery or AC powered
Smoke and CO detectors outside each sleeping area and within 10 feet of bedrooms
Basement smoke detector as close to the stairwell as possible, not near the furnace; smoke detector in the stairwell to a finished attic
Smoke detectors in the common areas of two family homes
Occupied attics (where permitted): exterior flashing strobe connected to the smoke detectors at the roof peak on the street side (City Ordinance 125-3 L)
The City's current requirements sheet and form still call for a mounted, charged 2A-10BC fire extinguisher in or within 10 feet of the kitchen

authorities.name: City of Passaic Fire Prevention Bureau (Passaic Fire Department)
authorities.lead_time: Submitted with the Occupancy Certificate application (apply at least 2 weeks before closing). The certification is valid 3 months after approval.

fire_cert.notes: The Passaic Fire Department's Fire Prevention Bureau is the fire code enforcing agency and inspects smoke and CO alarms as part of the Occupancy Certificate process; its fee ($45.00 initial, $25.00 re-inspection) is separate from the Division of Housing certificate fee. A 90-day temporary certification can be issued. The City's 2026 fire certification form and requirements sheet still check for a fire extinguisher even though P.L.2025, c.19 removed it from the state sale certificate; confirm with the Bureau. Three-family and larger buildings need a hardwired common-area fire alarm system with an NFPA 72 report.
